title: Make fractions, decimals and algebra agree
chapter: Make fractions, decimals and algebra agree
goal: Worked example: equal trays, each with a pouch and loose counters.

scenes.visual: Three identical trays. Each holds one pouch and 2 loose counters. Total label: 21 counters. Question: "How many counters are in each pouch?"
scenes.narration: Three identical trays each hold one pouch and two loose counters. Every pouch holds the same number of counters. Altogether the trays contain twenty-one counters. How many counters are in each pouch?

scenes.visual: A bar of length 21 splits into three equal parts labelled 7.
scenes.narration: The three trays are identical, so they share the twenty-one counters equally. Twenty-one divided by three is seven. Each tray holds seven counters.

scenes.visual: One tray's bar of 7 splits into a pouch part and 2 loose counters. The pouch part is labelled 5.
scenes.narration: In one tray, two of the seven counters are loose. The rest are in the pouch. Seven minus two is five. Each pouch holds five counters.

scenes.visual: Equation form appears beside the bars: 3 lots of (pouch and 2) is 21; pouch and 2 is 7; pouch is 5.
scenes.narration: In symbols: three lots of a pouch plus two equals twenty-one. So a pouch plus two equals seven, and a pouch equals five. The bars and the equation tell the same story.

scenes.visual: A second route: remove the 6 loose counters first, leaving 15 for three pouches.
scenes.narration: There is a second route. Take away all six loose counters first. Fifteen counters remain, shared by three pouches: five each. Two different orders, the same answer, which is a good check.

scenes.visual: Line: "share first, or remove the extras first". Notebook prompt.
scenes.narration: You can share first, or remove the extras first. Rebuild both routes, then try this: four identical bags each hold one box and three loose marbles, making forty marbles altogether. How many marbles are in each box?

notebook_exercise: Four bags each hold one box and 3 loose marbles; 40 marbles altogether. How many in each box?
